methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $356M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Gatik is a Series C autonomous transportation company that has raised $356M to date. The broader frontier-transportation sector includes eight private peers (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, ZeroAvia among others) and no direct public comparables, limiting traditional peer-median triangulation.

The stage-progression method is applicable here. Using total capital raised ($356M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement produces an implied valuation of $605M. This reflects the step-change in capital intensity and market validation expected between Series C and later institutional rounds. The peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow frontier-transportation universe—while the sector contains several players, none clustered sufficiently around Gatik's stage and scale to support a reliable median.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $514M to $695M, with $605M as the central estimate. This range reflects ±15% bandwidth around the stage-progression midpoint. Key uncertainties include (1) the appropriateness of the 1.7x multiplier in a nascent, capital-intensive sector where step-ups vary widely, and (2) the absence of market-tested peer valuations in autonomous last-mile delivery, limiting confidence in the proxy. Gatik's fundraising trajectory ($356M raised) supports the upper end of typical Series C scale, but validation against public-market or late-stage private transactions remains constrained.
